narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate that oil contributes a negligible portion to Dubai's GDP today.

units.meaning: Oil accounts for 0.3% of Dubai's GDP today.

basis.note: Table value is 0.3 in % units; relative_value 0.003 confirms 0.3%.

accepted_routes: Oil's share of GDP is about 0.3%.
Oil contributes roughly one-third of one percent of GDP.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The oil slice/segment or an on-screen label must display 0.3% (or an equivalent rounded statement such as about 0.3%).
units.temporal_anchor: today it only accounts for ... of its GDP
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the exact 0.3% oil share, or is the <1% threshold sufficient?

units.meaning: Oil's share is below the 1% threshold: less than 1% of Dubai's GDP.

basis.note: 0.3 is below the table note/narration threshold of less than 1%.

accepted_routes: Oil accounts for less than 1% of GDP.
Oil's GDP share is below one percent.
Not even 1% of Dubai's GDP comes from oil.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A visible annotation or label must state 'less than 1%' or show a 1% reference line/benchmark with the oil value below it.
units.temporal_anchor: today it only accounts for less than 1% of its GDP
units.reviewer_question: Is the qualitative '<1%' threshold required independently of the exact 0.3% value?

basis.note: Table value is 99.7 in % units; relative_value 0.997 confirms 99.7%.

accepted_routes: The rest of Dubai's GDP accounts for 99.7%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The non-oil slice or complement label must display 99.7%, or the chart must clearly show the rest of the pie making up nearly all GDP.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly give the non-oil complement value, or is showing only oil's tiny share enough?

units.meaning: Non-oil GDP share vastly exceeds oil's share: the gap is 99.4 percentage points, or non-oil is about 332 times oil's share.
accepted_routes: Non-oil's share is about 332 times oil's share.
Oil's share is roughly 1/332 of non-oil's share.
Oil is 99.4 percentage points below non-oil.
The gap between non-oil and oil is 99.4 percentage points.
units.visual_evidence_rule: If used, the chart or annotation must compare the two shares directly, e.g., 0.3% vs 99.7%, a 99.4-point gap, or a ~332x ratio. It should not imply 0.3% of non-oil GDP.
units.temporal_anchor: today it only accounts for less than 1% of its GDP
units.reviewer_question: Is a direct oil-vs-non-oil ratio/difference annotation required, or is showing the two shares side by side sufficient?

units.meaning: Oil and non-oil shares are complementary and sum to 100% of Dubai's GDP.
accepted_routes: Oil plus non-oil equals 100% of GDP.
The two shares together sum to 100%.
The pie covers all of Dubai's GDP with no missing slice.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The pie/bar must have exactly the two complementary categories Oil and Rest of GDP (non-oil), with no unexplained remainder; a sum-to-100 annotation can appear.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly state that the shares sum to 100%, or is this implicit in the pie/complement chart?

optional_valid: Dubai does have oil, but it is a tiny GDP category; this identity statement is valid only if it is not confused with oil being a large share.
A visual 1% benchmark line is optional if the text already clearly says oil is less than 1%.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims about economic diversification or oil causing non-oil growth.
Historical trends, future projections, or dates not in the table.
Dollar GDP amounts, total GDP figures, or other sector breakdowns.
Saying oil is 0% of GDP or that Dubai has no oil.
Comparing oil to non-oil GDP using the wrong denominator, e.g., 0.3% of non-oil GDP.
Claiming oil is exactly 1% of GDP.
notes: The table gives only two shares, so all numeric claims should stay within 0.3%, 99.7%, and derived <1%, 99.4 pp, ~332x, or 100% sum. Do not add years, GDP dollar amounts, other sectors, or causal claims about diversification.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
